s: Word Kitchen: A Walk Through Nature
Hello and welcome back to Word Kitchen, everyone!
Today we are cooking something different.
Today our ten new words are all about nature and the environment.
When I was a child, my grandmother had a house near a river.
In the summer, we sat by the river every day.
A river is a long line of water that moves to the sea.
My father taught me to swim in a river when I was eight years old.
I also remember a small bridge over that river.
We crossed the river on the bridge, and the water was so clear.
And next to that river, was there a forest?
A big forest was just behind the house.
A forest is a big place with many trees.
We walked into the forest every morning.
I love walking in a forest.
The air in a forest is fresh and clean.
In the forest, the trees are so tall that you cannot see the sky.
And in the morning, the forest is quiet.
But be careful in a forest at night.
It can be dark and a little scary.
Now let us talk about high places.
A mountain is a very high hill of rock.
Oh, I climbed a small mountain last year!
The mountain was not very high, but the view from the top was amazing.
I have never climbed a mountain.
On the mountain, we saw snow.
And far away, we could see the ocean.
An ocean is the big sea around the land.
I love the ocean because it never ends.
When you stand by the ocean, the ocean looks bigger than everything.
The sound of the ocean is so relaxing.
Last summer I sat on the beach for three hours and just listened to the ocean.
The ocean makes me feel small, but in a good way.
Now, let us move from big places to small things.
A flower is the colored part of a plant.
My sister grows flowers on her balcony.
Red flowers, yellow flowers, pink flowers.
I bought a flower for my mother yesterday.
One small flower, but she smiled for a long time.
A flower is a small gift with a big meaning.
And next to every flower, you find our sixth word, leaf.
A leaf is a flat green part of a plant or a tree.
In the autumn, the leaves change color.
A green leaf becomes yellow or red.
I love picking up a beautiful leaf when I walk.
In the park near my house, every leaf on the ground is like a small carpet.
And look, a new leaf is growing on this tree now.
When a leaf falls from a tree, it is dry.
Kids love to play with a dry leaf.
A leaf is flat and light.
Rain is water that falls from the sky.
I like the rain when I am at home.
The rain on the window makes a nice sound.
But I do not like rain when I forget my umbrella.
The rain was so strong that the street became a small river.
So the rain made the street look like a river.
And our eighth word is wind.
When the wind is strong, the trees dance.
The wind can be cold or warm.
Yesterday the wind was warm, and it felt like summer.
Today the wind is cold, so I need a jacket.
In my city, the wind is always strong in March.
The wind moves the clouds, and the wind makes the flags fly.
Speaking of clouds, let us do our ninth word first.
Sand is very small pieces of rock on the beach.
I love walking on warm sand.
When I was a child, I built castles with sand every summer.
And warm sand is the best place to sit and watch the ocean.
The sand was hot, the ocean was cool.
The sand on some beaches is white, and on other beaches the sand is black.
And now our last word, cloud.
A cloud is soft white water floating in the sky.
That cloud looks like a rabbit.
That small cloud looks like a boat.
I love watching the clouds move.
When a cloud covers the sun, it gets cooler.
When the cloud goes away, the sun is warm again.
Let us review our ten words quickly.
River, forest, mountain, ocean, flower, leaf, rain, wind, sand, cloud.
River, forest, mountain, ocean, flower, leaf, rain, wind, sand, cloud.
Go outside this weekend and find these things in nature.
And use your new words when you talk about them.
See you next time on Word Kitchen!
